name: AKU Board of Trustees' visit to Dar es Salaam

content.title: AKU Board of Trustees' visit to Dar es Salaam
content.summary: AKU Board of Trustees visits Dar es Salaam, Tanzania and spends a day with the faculty and students of IED, EA.

content.text: On Friday August 1, the Salama House, home to the Aga Khan University, Institute for Educational Development, East Africa was heaving with activity and was most definitely not 'business as usual' as it hosted the Aga Khan University's Board of Trustees. The trustees took a day out of their scheduled visit to Tanzania and spent it interacting with the students and faculty of the entities based in Dar es Salaam - the Institute for Educational Development, East Africa and the Faculty of Health Sciences (School of Nursing and Midwifery and the Medical College). This was done formally in a series of extensive discussions and continued informally over lunch.

The exhibition was inaugurated by Vice Provost of East Africa, Dr Kweku Bentil. He expressed his gratitude to all those who had made an effort to make the day a success. Each of the entity heads in East Africa including the Dean of the Medical College, Dean of the School of Nursing and Midwifery and the Director of the Institute for Educational Development introduced the presentations.

The occasion saw all entities present at an exhibition to showcase their recent achievements in research and teaching, and funded programmes and grants. Faculty and staff had worked collaboratively in the days leading up to the visit of the Board of Trustees to ensure that they had been able to display the breadth of the exciting work the University is engaged in across the East African region. The displays were very well received by the guests including President Firoz Rasul, Provost Professor Greg Moran, Vice-Provost Professor Kweku Bentil, Vice President HR Carol Ariano, Director General Al-Karim Haji and Dean of Research and Graduate Studies, Professor El-Nasir Lalani.

SONAM focused on the impact their graduates were making in the community including the implementation of Milieu therapy and Kangaroo mother care. The PGME programme had posters depicting a timeline that reflected how AKU had progressed in Tanzania. IED, EA focused its work through its four special interest groups: ICT in Education, Research and Development; Special Interest Group in Mathematics and Science Education; Early Years' Education; and Educational Leadership and Management and Gender and Widening Participation. The academic support offices including the library, the Project's Office and the Marketing and Communications office also put up displays.
